title_en: Golf (Nanjing) Real Estate Co., Ltd. v. Wu Yongmei — dispute over a heat supply contract
ruling_gist_en: In areas not covered by central heating, where a developer sells commercial housing to owners with heating facilities and agrees to provide heating services to the owners, the developer bears a compulsory duty to contract. The decision to terminate the heating supply contract shall be made by the owners or the owners' assembly.

Wu Yongmei for dispute over heat supply contract
full_text_en:
Golf (Nanjing) Real Estate Co., Ltd. v. Wu Yongmei — dispute over a heating supply contract

【Ruling Summary】

In a non-centralized heating supply area, where a developer sells commercial housing containing heating facilities to property owners and agrees to supply heating to the property owners, the developer is under a compulsory duty to contract, and the decision on whether to terminate the heating supply contract shall be made by the property owner or the property owners' assembly.

Plaintiff: Golf (Nanjing) Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Liyuan Middle Road, Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Huang Lijia, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Wu Yongmei, female, 57 years old, residing at Xiaoshi Village, Xiaquan District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Golf (Nanjing) Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Golf Company), filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Jiangning District, Nanjing, against the defendant, Wu Yongmei, concerning a dispute over a heating supply contract.

The plaintiff, Golf Company, alleged: On June 24, 2007, the plaintiff and the defendant, Wu Yongmei, entered into a "Golf International Garden Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contract," under which Wu Yongmei purchased one unit of housing, No. 401, Building 10, Golf International Garden, developed and constructed by the plaintiff, with an area of 152.67 square meters. Article (4) of the appendix to the contract, "Other Agreements Between Party A and Party B," stipulated: The property owner agrees to pay a basic fee of RMB 4.2 per square meter per month according to the building area during the heating season, and a hot water energy fee of RMB 0.7 per square meter per month according to the building area during the non-heating season. The annual heating season runs from November 16 to March 15 of the following year, with the remainder being the non-heating season. Since June 2008, the plaintiff had provided heating supply to Wu Yongmei on a substitute basis. Subsequently, Wu Yongmei paid heating fees at the rate of RMB 7 per square meter per month during the heating season and RMB 0.7 per square meter per month during the non-heating season until December 31, 2010. On January 9, 2011, Wu Yongmei submitted to the plaintiff a "Report on Application for Suspension of Heating and Hot Water Use," requesting termination of the heating supply relationship between the parties. The plaintiff now requests the court to: 1. Confirm that the substitute heating supply relationship between the parties has been terminated; 2. Order Wu Yongmei to pay basic heating fees of RMB 5,183 (from January 1, 2011 to April 30, 2012).

The defendant, Wu Yongmei, argued: The defendant did submit to the plaintiff, Golf Company, a "Report on Application for Suspension of Heating and Hot Water Use" requesting suspension of heating and hot water use; however, the report did not seek to terminate the heating supply relationship with Golf Company, and therefore the defendant does not agree to terminate the heating supply contract between the parties. The defendant has applied for suspension of heating and hot water use and has in fact not used the heating or hot water supplied by Golf Company, so the defendant should not be required to pay heating fees to Golf Company. In summary, the defendant requests that the court dismiss Golf Company's claims.

The People's Court of Jiangning District, Nanjing, found at first instance:

On June 24, 2007, the plaintiff, Golf Company, and the defendant, Wu Yongmei, together with Hao Zheng (Wu Yongmei's husband, now deceased), entered into a "Golf International Garden Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Pre-sale Contract"), stipulating: Golf Company sold to Wu Yongmei and Hao Zheng one unit of housing, No. 401, Building 10, Golf International Garden, located at No. 88 Liyuan Middle Road, Jiangning District, Nanjing (hereinafter referred to as Unit 401). The appendix to the contract, "Other Agreements Between Party A and Party B," stipulated: The use and maintenance of the floor heating equipment shall be formulated in accordance with the contracts and relevant standards of the thermal power plant, and the property owner must strictly comply. To consider the interests of all property owners and the quality standards of the community, regardless of whether the property owner resides in the unit, the property owner shall fulfill the obligation to pay fees. Before the establishment of the property owners' committee, the property owner shall pay a basic fee of RMB 4.2 per square meter per month according to the building area during the heating season, plus a usage metering fee, with the meter fee calculated separately and capped at RMB 2.8; and a hot water energy fee of RMB 0.7 per square meter per month according to the building area during the non-heating season. The above fees shall be collected and managed by the property management company on a substitute basis. Prices shall fluctuate with the cost of goods. The general principle for fee collection is that 60% is calculated based on area and 40% is calculated based on usage. Starting in 2008, Golf Company began supplying heating and hot water to the Golf International Garden community. On January 9, 2011, Wu Yongmei submitted to Golf Company a "Report on Application for Suspension of Heating and Hot Water Use," stating: The owner of Unit 401 applies for suspension of the hot water and heating supplied by the community as of January 9, 2011. On January 25, 2011, Wu Yongmei paid Golf Company heating fees of RMB 1,815.2 for the period from March 16, 2010 to December 31, 2010, at the rate of RMB 7 per square meter per month during the heating season and RMB 0.7 per square meter per month during the non-heating season.

It was also found that the measured building area of Unit 401 is 155.59 square meters, and the ownership is currently registered in the name of the defendant, Wu Yongmei.

During the trial, the plaintiff, Golf Company, stated that the heating fees it collected included the costs of hot water and heating as well as the maintenance costs of the heating equipment; the cost of supplying heating to the community property owners was already far higher than the heating fees collected from them. The heating fees claimed by Golf Company in this case against the defendant, Wu Yongmei, for the heating season were 60% of the normal standard, which already took into account Wu Yongmei's suspension of hot water and heating use. Wu Yongmei also acknowledged that the cost of heating supplied by Golf Company was higher than the heating fees collected.

The issues in dispute at first instance were: First, whether the plaintiff, Golf Company, could terminate the heating supply contract between itself and the defendant, Wu Yongmei; Second, whether the defendant, Wu Yongmei, was obligated to pay heating fees to the plaintiff, Golf Company, after applying for suspension of heating.

The People's Court of Jiangning District, Nanjing, held at first instance:

The "Pre-sale Contract" entered into between the plaintiff, Golf Company, and the defendant, Wu Yongmei, represented the true intentions of both parties, is lawful and valid, and is protected by law; both parties shall perform their obligations in accordance with the contract. In the sales contract, the parties not only specifically agreed on the terms for the sale of the commercial housing, but also agreed on the timing and usage fees for heating and hot water supply, explicitly stipulating that Golf Company was obligated to supply heating and hot water, and Wu Yongmei was obligated to pay the usage fees in accordance with the standards. Therefore, a heating supply contract relationship was formed between Golf Company and Wu Yongmei. With respect to Golf Company's request to confirm that the substitute heating supply relationship between the parties had been terminated, because Wu Yongmei's report on suspension of heating and hot water only requested suspension of hot water and heating use, not termination of the heating supply contract between the parties, and during trial Wu Yongmei did not agree to terminate the heating supply contract between them, and moreover, the heating and hot water supply services provided by Golf Company were for all property owners of the Golf International Garden community; the relevant facilities are public facilities of the community's property owners. Terminating the heating supply contract would inevitably affect the value of Wu Yongmei's housing unit and the legitimate rights and interests of other property owners. The decision on whether to terminate the heating supply should be made by the property owners' assembly. Therefore, this court does not support Golf Company's request on this matter. Regarding the heating fees claimed by Golf Company, because such fees include not only the costs of heating and hot water but also the maintenance costs of the heating equipment, although Wu Yongmei applied for suspension of heating and hot water, she should still pay the maintenance costs of the heating equipment. Combined with the fact that Wu Yongmei also acknowledged that the cost of heating supplied by Golf Company was higher than the heating fees collected, and that Wu Yongmei had paid heating fees to Golf Company for the period from March 16, 2010 to December 31, 2010, at the rate of RMB 7 per square meter per month during the heating season and RMB 0.7 per square meter per month during the non-heating season, it should be considered that both parties had modified the standard for heating fees agreed in the "Pre-sale Contract." This court determines that Wu Yongmei shall pay heating fees to Golf Company at 60% of the payment standard for 2010 heating fees paid by her, which calculates to RMB 4,777. Accordingly, the court partially supports Golf Company's claim for heating fees.

For these reasons, in accordance with Article 44, Article 93, Article 94, and Article 184 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court of Jiangning District, Nanjing, rendered the following judgment on June 14, 2012:

I. The defendant, Wu Yongmei, shall pay the plaintiff, Golf Company, heating fees of RMB 4,777 for the period from January 1, 2011 to April 30, 2012, to be paid in full within 10 days of the date this judgment takes legal effect.

II. The other claims of the plaintiff, Golf Company, are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed within the statutory period, and the judgment has taken legal effect.
